text:
alex: auth-monitor alerted — sudden surge of SSO logins over the last 4m. ~90 auths across 12 distinct accounts. Device_fingerprint header is rotating (dfp-*) and UA is mostly identical. IPs are a mix of low-volume residential ranges + a couple cloud proxies.

maria: :eyes: can you dump a sample? any MFA successes/failures?

alex: sample below. MFA succeeded on 8 accounts, failed/prompted repeatedly on the others (lots of push retries). snippet: ```
user: jdoe@example.com | ip: 54.23.12.45 | device_fingerprint: dfp-7a2b | ua: Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh) AppleWebKit/537.36 | mfa: success
user: sally@example.com | ip: 3.15.200.10 | device_fingerprint: dfp-9f1c | ua: Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh) AppleWebKit/537.36 | mfa: prompt-flood
user: ops+svc@example.com | ip: 84.46.23.7 | device_fingerprint: dfp-0a0d | ua: Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh) AppleWebKit/537.36 | mfa: blocked
```

priya: pattern looks like credential stuffing with device spoofing + MFA fatigue (push flood). are these customer admin accounts? any Dedicated tenants impacted?

alex: 3 are admin-level, 2 are service accounts with long-lived tokens (we saw session refreshes). Dedicated tenants? none listed in the sample, just standard prod users.

sam: Oncall for auth here — immediate steps: 1) block the most frequent IPs at WAF, 2) add temporary rate-limit on SSO endpoint for suspicious device_fingerprint header, 3) revoke active sessions for the 12 accounts, 4) enable forced password reset for affected accounts if there are successful logins. I'll run these now.

maria: +1 to session revokes. also add device_fingerprint to the denylist if repeating pattern. we should avoid full org-wide password resets unless we see broad compromise.

jin: I'm checking audit logs in CloudLogging and KMS access. KMS decrypts don't show anomalies. service-account keys look unused aside from normal CI jobs. forwarding logs to sec-archive.

auth-bot: [alert] auth-monitor: high device-fingerprint churn detected (score 0.92) — https://internal.redwood/alerts/17283456

priya: timeline: last successful admin MFA was 02:08 UTC, attack window 02:04–02:12 UTC. Looks automated. Could be an abused credential list + device spoofing library.

alex: containment done: blocked 5 IPs on WAF, applied 30s rate-limit per device_fingerprint, revoked sessions for the 12 accounts, forced MFA re-enroll for 2 admin accounts. Notifying affected users via support.

maria: good. next: prepare comms for infra and customer-facing? security incident? severity probably P2 unless we find exfil.

sam: also pushed a quick rule to reject device_fingerprint values matching regex `^dfp-[0-9a-f]{4}$` for now (whitelist approach later). This is a blunt hammer but reduces noise.

jin: pulled full audit for the 12 accounts — no data download events, no KMS key use anomalies. service tokens rotated? one service account performed a token refresh at 02:06 — looks like normal refresh.

priya: action items for post-mortem: 1) add runbook entry for rotating device_fingerprint attacks, 2) create more granular RBAC alert when admin accounts see unusual device entropy, 3) add MFA push rate-limiting and anti-automation heuristics, 4) update detection rules to correlate UA similarity + fingerprint churn + geo hops.

alex: I'm drafting a short incident summary for leadership and legal. Will include affected accounts, containment, and recommended mitigations.

maria: please include timeline and evidence that KMS and data access were not abused. attach audit exports.

sam: I'll follow up with infra to add a WAF signature and coordinate a repo PR for the temporary denylist.

priya: assign owner for postmortem and remediation tracking? suggest @maria.

maria: happy to own. will create a postmortem doc and invite eng, devex, and support.

alex: notes for postmortem: consider forcing password rotations for accounts showing multiple failed MFA prompts; consider hardening SSO throttles; evaluate tighter RBAC on service accounts that don't need interactive SSO.

jin: I've exported logs to secure bucket and uploaded to the incident folder s3://redwood-sec-archive/1728345600/ — shared with incident channel.

auth-bot: [info] ticket created: SEC-2024-0985 — incident triage in progress

maria: thanks all. we'll reconvene after I have the doc. If anyone finds evidence of exfil, ping sec-oncall immediately. :thumbsup:

sam: closing the live thread — monitoring for reoccurrence and tuning rules.

alex: thanks — nice triage everyone.
